actor_population.observed: each iteration reads a runtime-array byte, skips bit 20 entries, uses low 5 bits as an index into the team data path, then advances actor and source positions

active_player_mask.observed: for each team, entries after the configured active-player count are ORed with bit 20 and remaining entries are ANDed with DF; slot zero of each 20-byte array is not traversed by this routine

trajectory_selection_compare.guard: runs only when the player-setting value is below 4 and the corresponding selector word 1E6C/1E6E is non-negative
trajectory_selection_compare.comparison: CODE_83:C74F scans 11 snapshot byte positions, excludes a snapshot candidate with bit 20, searches its value in the current array, and writes a two-byte selection pair through the supplied selector-word pointer

selection_pair.low_byte: current-array byte offset found by the second search
selection_pair.high_byte: snapshot candidate value found missing from the current array
selection_pair.consumer: CODE_83:C7CB reads the low byte to index the current runtime array; CODE_83:C870 reads the high byte after XBA

limitations: The arrays are runtime state and may be modified after initialization; this does not freeze a final formation or lineup.
The low-five-bit index, bit-20 activity mask, and trajectory comparison are structural observations, not player-number, control, pass, or shot semantics.
The selector pair has not been given gameplay labels; this extraction does not identify a transition as a pass, shot, player switch, or formation event.
No web roster movement or actor spawning behavior is changed from this extraction alone.
